line: I was in the coke spot Makaveli on repeat, startin’ to think that I know Pac
vault_lines: I was in the coke spot
meaning: Dave recalls being in the coke spot probably selling dope and listening to a ton of Makaveli, one of 2pacs aliases. So much he almost feels like he knew him.

line: I been real paranoid in the streets, every night gotta clutch it in my dreams
vault_lines: I been real paranoid in the streets, every night gotta clutch it in my dreams
meaning: Herbo is probably suffering from PTSD due to the violence that goes on outside his four walls. In turn, he sleeps with a weapon to aid his paranoia. I believe kendrick warned us about that, though.

line: I can tell if you gang by the door knock
vault_lines: I can tell if you gang by the door knock
meaning: Herb can tells if you gang by the door knock

line: Baking soda in the kitchen gettin’ busy with my mans Kinda dizzy in this bitch, breathin’ wiffles of the tan Fuck around, catch a high, startin’ to stumble where I stand
vault_lines: Baking soda in the kitchen gettin' busy with my mans
meaning: While cooking crack, also known as “tan” because of its color when cut with fillers,  Herb accidentally sniffs some of the fumes. This causes Herb to catch a contact high and he starts stumbling due to the drug’s side effects.

line: I go to Texas, they treat a nigga like a Maverick
vault_lines: I go to Texas, they treat a nigga like a Maverick
meaning: Dave East references the state of Texas and in particular the NBA franchise Dallas Mavericks. Despite being born in Harlem, New York, East likens the treatment he receives in the state of Texas to that of the players on the Dallas Mavericks.

line: My bitches was boostin’, go to canal and come back uptown with a lot (Hey baby)
vault_lines: My bitches was boostin', go to canal and come back uptown with a lot (Hey baby)
meaning:
“ Boostin' ” is when you steal retail items from and resell it on your own or to a local business for profit.

In the book God-Level Knowledge Darts: Life Lessons from the Bronx by comedic duo Desus Nice and The Kid Mero (also known as the Bodega Boys) the subject of boosting is talked about in the chapter “Crime and Punishment” :

“ ….A major part of the graffiti culture I grew up in was boosting. We called it racking and n—- was out here racking everything, paint, $500 fuckin North Face spelunking space jackets, food. We had a system and deals in place with bodegas and little independent shops where you would rack some shit they paid mad money for wholesale and sell it to them for half that….” (p.109)

line: Stuffing clips downwards in my jeans ’cause my mom’s near
vault_lines: Stuffing clips downwards in my jeans 'cause my mom's near
meaning: G Herbo is saying that he stuffed magazines, which is the definition of a clip, of bullets in his jeans because his mom was around. He hid his illegal and dangerous tools so his mom wouldn’t reprimand him.

line: The FED’s on me now every monday the car switch
vault_lines: The FED's on me now every monday the car switch
meaning: The FEDs is a commonly used modern name for the police. Dave East is saying that since the police are hunting him down, he switches his car to avoid identification.

line: I skipped right to Balmain ain’t copped too many Nudie’s
vault_lines: I skipped right to Balmain ain't copped too many Nudie's
meaning:
Dave East didn’t waste any time purchasing Nudie jeans, he instead jumped right to the very popular and pricey Balmain jeans.

Balmain is one of Dave’s favorite designer brands, as he has mentioned the French brand in other songs such as, “Keisha”:

15,000 in my Balmain’s, I’m lackin'

line: I was in the trenches, kicks red but I wasn’t bleeding
vault_lines: I was in the trenches, kicks red but I wasn't bleeding
meaning: G Herbo’s referring to Christian Louboutin sneakers, which have distinctly red bottoms. “I wasn’t bleeding” may also be his way of saying he’s not part of the Blood gang despite wearing red—Herbo’s affiliated with the “Every Body Killer” gang, and even wrote a song about it.

line: Fendi monster, my jacket looking like it’s staring at niggas
vault_lines: Fendi monster, my jacket looking like it's staring at niggas
meaning: Fendi Monster Jackets are known to have eyes on them.

line: I was popping blue devils, Coach K ain’t recruit me
vault_lines: I was popping blue devils, Coach K ain't recruit me
meaning:
Dave was heavy into drugs at an early age, instead of focusing on playing basketball. Therefore he knew he would never be recruited by the top programs like the Duke Blue Devils, coached by Mike Krzyzewski, commonly referred to as Coach K.

“Blue Devils” could be referring to ecstacy pills or Roxicodone tablets, commonly known as “Roxies”.
